language_task: pik up one objet from the big bowl and put inside the small box that is empty
outcome_evidence: The robot initially carries the loaded bowl rather than an individual object (right and top, frames 180-588), then extracts the spotted plush (left, right and top, frames 810-840). It repeatedly repositions that object and releases it onto the tabletop outside the boxes (for example, frames 1364-1375 and 1791-1799). At frame 1999, left, right and top show the plush still at the gripper beside the bowl, not inside a box. Thus unsuccessful transfers are visible and eventual completion remains unconfirmed; the recording ending does not establish abnormal termination. Both orange boxes appear empty in top, so the intended destination is not uniquely distinguishable, but neither receives the object.

failure_annotations.explanation: The robot displaces the bowl from frame 141 and lifts and carries the entire loaded container instead of extracting one object (left, right and top, frames 180, 300, 350, 480 and 570). This is continuous wrong-object handling across the window boundary, ending when lowering and release recovery begin around frame 588.
failure_annotations.recovery: Set the bowl down stably, release its rim, and grasp an individual object inside before transporting it to an empty small box; no human intervention is visibly needed.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The contents remain contained, with no visible spill, damage or harmful impact; the consequence is an unsuccessful task detour.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The held, displaced bowl needs straightforward lowering and release to restore a stable acquisition setup, without repair or human assistance.
